matches.rationale: Both identify selective reporting of FID scores in the abstract. GT1 notes the abstract claims 2.38-2.64 while omitting worse results (>3.6) at higher replacement ratios. Pred5 identifies the abstract claims 2.38-2.64 but questions the representativeness of this range given Table 4 data.

Both identify confusion in Equation 2's regression objective definition. GT2 notes ambiguity about L_reg and its relationship to L1/L2/Huber losses. Pred7 identifies the confusing notation where L_reg appears as both a function and a norm.

GT3 concerns missing hyperparameter details in Table C.1 (gradient clipping specification, warmup schedule details, batch size clarification). No finding addresses these specific omissions in the appendix table.

Both identify overstated claims about grafting's generality. GT4 notes the introduction overstates utility with absolute language despite limited testing. Pred3 identifies the conclusion's extreme claims about 'completely solves' and 'universally outperforms' being unsupported.

Both identify issues with Table 4's selective reporting. GT5 notes the use of '✗' without actual FID values and ambiguity in ΔFLOPs columns. Pred4 identifies the same issue where failed experiments (✗) still report efficiency metrics.

Both identify fabricated relevance of the plant grafting reference. GT6 notes Reference [4] is a plant biology paper misattributed as inspiring the computational method. Pred9 identifies the same issue with the footnote claiming Goldschmidt discusses neural network concepts.
GT7 concerns the interpretation of the L_k locality metric and whether L_k > 0.5 truly indicates local attention patterns. No finding addresses this specific methodological interpretation issue.

GT8 concerns unfair comparison in PixArt-Σ evaluation (different sampling steps or LoRA vs full finetuning for baseline). No finding addresses these specific experimental protocol issues for the baseline comparison.

Both identify misleading claims about the depth-to-width model. GT9 notes the claim of 'outperforms' is misleading due to 2× parameter difference. Pred2 identifies the contradiction where the text claims it 'surpasses' baseline (FID 2.27) but actually achieves worse FID (2.77).

GT10 concerns omission of limitations and failure cases in the conclusion. While Pred3 identifies overstated claims in the conclusion, it doesn't specifically address the ethical issue of omitting known limitations and biases.

GT11 concerns selective latency reporting at batch size=2 for PixArt-Σ. Pred1 identifies the 1.43× speedup discrepancy in Table 5. Pred6 identifies the batch size=2 speedup measurement issue and footnote contradiction about large batch sizes.

GT12 concerns the inconsistency between abstract's '<2% compute' claim and the actual best results requiring 20% data (not 10%). No finding addresses this specific data percentage inconsistency between abstract and Figure 4(a).
GT13 concerns inappropriate promotional language ('revolutionary,' 'paradigm shift,' 'unprecedented') in the introduction. No finding identifies this specific rhetorical manipulation issue.
GT14 concerns incorrect FLOP calculation formulas in Section H.1 and inconsistencies with reported ΔFLOPs reductions. No finding addresses these specific mathematical errors in the appendix.

GT15 concerns misrepresentation of Reference [52] about progressive network grafting in Appendix A. While Pred9 identifies a citation issue, it concerns Reference [4] (plant grafting), not Reference [52] (few-shot knowledge distillation).
